method_card.title: How to Find the nth Term of a Linear Sequence
method_card.content:
A linear sequence goes up or down by the same amount each time. That fixed step is the common difference \(d\).

The nth term is \(T(n) = dn + c\). Find \(d\) by subtracting consecutive terms, then the constant \(c = \text{first term} - d\).

To find a term, substitute its position \(n\). To test whether a number is in the sequence, set \(dn + c\) equal to it and solve: a positive whole-number \(n\) means it is a term.
method_card.example:
Find the nth term of 5, 8, 11, 14, ...

Step 1: Common difference \(d = 8 - 5 = 3\)

Step 2: \(3n\) part: 3, 6, 9, 12, ...

Step 3: Constant: \(5 - 3 = 2\)

Answer: \(T(n) = 3n + 2\)

Check: \(T(1) = 3(1) + 2 = 5\) ✔, \(T(2) = 3(2) + 2 = 8\) ✔

steps: To find which term has a value, set \(dn + c\) equal to it and solve for \(n\).
